member.name: T:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Assembly.MetadataImporter
member.summary: A metadata importer that keeps the processed module corlib-consistent. The Cecil imports references scoped to the assembly that actually defines a member. When a type is resolved through the .NET Standard facade, the definition lives in the underlying runtime library (e.g. 'mscorlib'), so importing members of that definition would inject a second corlib reference ('mscorlib' next to 'netstandard') into the target module. A dual-corlib module corrupts the UnityLinker netstandard facade retargeting and fails the IL2CPP build with a MissingAssemblyException. This importer redirects any imported corlib scope to the core library the target module already references, so the module always keeps a single, consistent corlib.

member.name: F:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Assembly.MetadataImporter.CorlibNames
member.summary: Fast lookup set of the known core library assembly names, built from the shared . Any imported scope matching one of these is a corlib and gets redirected.

member.param: The assembly name reference to import.
member.returns: The imported assembly name reference, redirected to the module corlib if applicable.

member.name: T:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Assembly.ReflectionImporter
member.summary: A reflection importer that keeps the processed module corlib-consistent. The Cecil imports System types from the runtime hosting the obfuscator (the Unity Editor Mono runtime, whose core library is 'mscorlib'). For player assemblies compiled against .NET Standard, this would inject a second corlib reference ('mscorlib' next to 'netstandard'), which corrupts the UnityLinker netstandard facade retargeting and fails the IL2CPP build with a MissingAssemblyException. member.name: T:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Compatibility.Component.UIToolkitCompatibilityComponent
member.summary:
Component for Unity UI Toolkit (UIElements) compatibility.
Custom UI Toolkit controls are referenced by their fully-qualified type name from UXML assets: - Unity 2021/2022 (and 2023.1) register custom controls through nested 'UxmlFactory' / 'UxmlTraits' classes, whose default UXML name is the fully-qualified name of the control type. - Unity 2023.2+ / Unity 6 register custom controls through the '[UxmlElement]' / '[UxmlObject]' attributes and source generation, which is also based on the fully-qualified type name. Attributes exposed to UXML / the UI Builder are marked with '[UxmlAttribute]'.

member.name: T:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Compatibility.Addressable.AddressableBackupStore
member.summary:
Persists pristine (un-obfuscated) copies of addressable bundle files together with a small state file, so that incremental Addressables builds which reuse already-obfuscated bundles can be detected and the pristine bundle restored before it is obfuscated again with the current build's rename mapping.
One store exists per processed bundle build directory (local and remote each get their own). The store lives in Unity's project Library directory () under 'Addressables/Backup/[hash-of-build-path]/', which is never imported by Unity, persists across editor sessions and is excluded from version control.

member.name: T:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Compatibility.Addressable.AesHelper
member.summary:
Stateless helper around AES-256 in CBC mode with PKCS7 padding.
All operations are static and accept the key and IV as parameters; the helper itself never retains key material. A fixed-size binary layout is provided so a key+IV pair can be appended to an encrypted addressable at a known offset and recovered on load.
Key size is fixed at 32 bytes (AES-256) and IV size at 16 bytes (AES block size), giving a constant of 48 bytes.

member.name: T:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Compatibility.LinkXmlComponent
member.summary: Generates an additional Unity linker file (link.xml) that preserves the obfuscated names of types that are preserved by the original link.xml files in the project. Because the obfuscator renames types after the user authored their link.xml files, the original preserve entries would no longer match and the UnityLinker could strip the renamed types. This component scans all link.xml files in the project (Assets and Packages), translates the type entries of obfuscated assemblies to their obfuscated names, and writes them into a single additional link.xml. The generated file is passed to the UnityLinker by the BuildPostProcessor via IUnityLinkerProcessor.GenerateAdditionalLinkXmlFile. The original link.xml files are never modified.

member.name: M:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Compatibility.LinkXmlComponent.BuildTypeRenameMapping
member.summary: Builds the mapping from original type full names to obfuscated type full names per assembly. Iterates all types of all obfuscated assemblies (from the original mapping) and resolves the obfuscated namespace, the obfuscated type name and the obfuscated names of all declaring types in the nested type chain from the current rename mapping. Only types whose full name actually changed are contained in the result.
member.returns: Assembly name -> (original type full name -> obfuscated type full name).

member.summary: Resolves the obfuscated full name of the type identified by . The full name of a nested type contains its declaring type chain separated by '/', so each segment is looked up individually in the current rename mapping. The namespace of the root segment is translated via the namespace mapping.
member.param: The original type key to resolve the obfuscated full name for.
The current mapping of original type keys to obfuscated type names.
The current mapping of original type keys to obfuscated namespaces.
member.returns: The obfuscated full name, which equals the original full name if nothing was renamed.

member.summary: Transforms a single link.xml file: for each assembly node of an obfuscated assembly, the type entries whose full name was renamed are written to with their obfuscated full name. The 'preserve' attributes of the assembly and type nodes are kept. Entries of not obfuscated assemblies and not renamed types are skipped, because the original link.xml files remain valid for them.
member.param: The path of the link.xml file to transform.
Assembly name -> (original type full name -> obfuscated type full name).
The names of all obfuscated assemblies.
The writer of the generated additional link.xml.
member.returns: The number of translated type entries.

member.name: T:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Security.AntiTamperingRuntime
member.summary:
Runtime anti-tampering protection system that performs integrity checks. Provides two separate entry points: InitializeMono for Mono builds and InitializeIL2CPP for IL2CPP builds. The build-time AntiTamperingComponent selects and clones the correct method based on the scripting backend.
Each method is fully self-contained (no cross-method calls, no static fields) because CloneHelper.TryToCloneMethod clones a single method and does not remap cross-method call targets.

member.name: M:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Security.AntiTamperingRuntime.InitializeMono
member.summary: Mono anti-tampering entry point. Validates the integrity of the managed assembly on disk by comparing its SHA256 hash against a stored reference hash in StreamingAssets/Cache. Uses Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly() and Assembly.Location to find the assembly file.

member.name: M:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Security.AntiTamperingRuntime.InitializeIL2CPP
member.summary: IL2CPP anti-tampering entry point. Validates the integrity of native binaries (GameAssembly, baselib, UnityPlayer) by comparing their SHA256 hashes against stored reference hashes in StreamingAssets/Cache. Does NOT use System.Reflection.Assembly (unreliable under IL2CPP). Uses Application.platform for extension/path resolution and Application.dataPath for binary locations.

member.summary: Computes the evaluation stack depth at the entry of every reachable instruction by propagating depths along the control flow graph (fall-through, branch targets and exception handler entries).
member.param: Method definition to analyze.
True if the containing method has a return value; otherwise, false.
member.returns: Mapping of each reachable instruction to its evaluation stack entry depth.

member.name: M:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssemblyBuild.Pipeline.Component.Security.ControlFlow.BlockParser.ComputeNoSplitInstructions(GUPS.Mono.Cecil.MethodDefinition,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{GUPS.Mono.Cecil.Cil.Instruction,System.Int32})
member.summary: Computes the set of instructions after which no block split may occur. Whenever a branch (or switch) targets an instruction that is entered with a non-empty evaluation stack (e.g. the dup/brtrue/pop pattern emitted for null propagation like 'array?.Length'), the branch and its target must end up in the same block. Otherwise the value passed on the evaluation stack would cross a block boundary, which produces invalid IL once the blocks are reordered by the control flow dispatcher. The whole lexical range between such a branch and its target is therefore marked as unsplittable.
member.param: Method definition to analyze.
Mapping of each reachable instruction to its evaluation stack entry depth.
member.returns: Set of instructions after which the parser must not split blocks.

member.summary: Assigns a unique random identifier to every block in the provided list. Uniqueness within the method is required so the control flow dispatcher can unambiguously distinguish blocks via their identifier comparisons.

member.summary: Rewrites a single method body into a dispatcher-based (control flow flattened) layout. The method is split into logical blocks by , the blocks are shuffled, and a switch-based dispatcher drives execution from one block to the next via a state variable. member.name: M:GUPS.Obfuscator.Editor.Project.PostAssetsBuild.Pipeline.Component.MonoBehaviourAssetsComponent.TryOverrideInPlayerDataCache(System.String,System.Func{System.String,System.Boolean})
member.summary: Locates the passed file in the player data cache and overrides it using the passed override method. All [Path]/Library/PlayerDataCache/[any]/Data/[_FileName] files are collected and exactly one is overridden: 1. The newest file in a directory of the current build target, named [Unity internal build target name] or [BuildTarget enum name], optionally followed by a number (for example "Win64", "Win642", "iOS2"). On an equal write time the higher number wins. 2. Otherwise the newest file in any directory. Only one target is built at a time, so the newest file belongs to the current build. Older (stale) files are not touched.
member.param: The file name to override (globalgamemanagers.assets or data.unity3d).
The override method to call with the resolved file path.
member.returns: True if the file was found and overridden successfully; false otherwise.
